# CFO Briefing — H1 2026 Close (as of 30/06/2026)

**Source:** `./finance` — ledger (86 entries, Jan–Jun 2026), chart of accounts, board notes/README.
All figures in BRL (R$).

## 1. How each month went

| Month | Revenue | Gross Margin % | EBITDA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026-01 | 200,510.87 | 70.0% | −210,278.96 |
| 2026-02 | 216,328.06 | 70.3% | −212,300.08 |
| 2026-03 | 219,066.17 | 68.5% | −204,525.45 |
| 2026-04 | 238,163.26 | 70.2% | −196,950.65 |
| 2026-05 | 243,032.89 | 69.6% | −201,945.82 |
| 2026-06 | 272,391.57 | 72.4% | −192,968.22 |

**Narrative:** Revenue grew every month — Jan→Jun +35.9% (CAGR ≈ 6.3%/mo). Gross margin dipped in
March (68.5%, cloud/GPU costs ahead of revenue) and finished June at the H1 high of 72.4%. EBITDA
is negative throughout but trending better: −212k (Feb trough) → −193k (Jun). The gap between
revenue growth (+71.9k Jan→Jun) and cost growth is narrowing monthly losses — the model is
converging toward breakeven, not yet at it.

## 2. Cash & runway (board definitions)

- Cash at 31/05/2026: **R$ 2,309,188.00** · Cash at 30/06/2026: **R$ 1,847,350.40**
- **Burn** = average monthly negative EBITDA of the last three closed months (Apr, May, Jun)
  = (196,950.65 + 201,945.82 + 192,968.22) / 3 = **R$ 197,288.23 / month**
- **Runway** = 1,847,350.40 / 197,288.23 = **9.4 months → cash out around 2027-03** (≈ March 2027)

Note: actual cash fell 461,837.60 in June — more than June's EBITDA burn of ~193k — meaning the
ledger covers P&L postings only (non-P&L outflows such as payroll taxes, capex, or debt are not in
this extract). Runway per the board's formula uses the official closing cash balance, so 9.4 months
stands as the governance number; if cash continued falling at June's actual rate (~462k/mo) the
hard floor would be ~4 months. Recommend the CFO flag this reconciliation to investors.

## 3. Assumptions & treatment

- Amounts/dates parsed as Brazilian format (dd/mm/yyyy; 1.234,56).
- **Revenue** = accounts 3.1.01 + 3.1.02 + 3.1.09 (the Kestrel refund is a contra-revenue per the
  chart of accounts, so it nets off March and May revenue).
- **Gross margin %** = (revenue − COGS incl. 4.1.01 cloud/GPUs + 4.1.02 support) / revenue.
- **EBITDA** excludes the financial block (6.1.01 investment income, 6.1.02 interest/IOF), per
  standard EBITDA definition. Including them would improve each month by ~+6.5k net — immaterial
  and not comparable.
- All 86 ledger entries fall inside Jan–Jun 2026; nothing out of scope, no unknown accounts.

## 4. Key takeaways for the investor meeting

1. Growth is real: +36% revenue in six months, margin at an H1 high in June.
2. Losses are shrinking but plateauing around −195k/mo; opex (engineering + sales) is ~2/3 of spend.
3. **Runway ≈ 9.4 months on the board's definition** — bridge is needed by year-end for a
   comfort-margin 2027 plan.
4. June's cash movement vs. P&L burn needs explanation (see §2) — get the full cash-flow statement
   before the meeting.


--- analyze.ps1 ---
# Parse Brazilian-format ledger and build H1 2026 monthly P&L
$lineOf = @{}
Import-Csv -Delimiter ';' finance/chart_of_accounts.csv | ForEach-Object { $lineOf[$_.account] = $_.pnl_line }

$rows = Import-Csv -Delimiter ';' finance/ledger.csv
$months = '2026-01','2026-02','2026-03','2026-04','2026-05','2026-06'
$agg = @{}
foreach ($m in $months) { $agg[$m] = @{revenue=0.0; cogs=0.0; sales_marketing=0.0; rnd=0.0; ga=0.0; financial=0.0} }

function ToNum($s) {
  # -56.661,03 -> -56661.03
  $neg = $s.StartsWith('-')
  $t = $s.TrimStart('-').Replace('.','').Replace(',','.')
  $v = [double]$t
  if ($neg) { $v = -$v }
  return $v
}

foreach ($r in $rows) {
  $d = $r.date -split '/'                      # dd/mm/yyyy
  $key = '{0}-{1}' -f $d[2], $d[1].PadLeft(2,'0')
  $line = $lineOf[$r.account]
  if (-not $line) { Write-Warning "Unknown account $($r.account)"; continue }
  if (-not $agg.ContainsKey($key)) { Write-Warning "Out of range date: $($r.date)"; continue }
  $agg[$key][$line] += ToNum $r.amount
}

$res = [ordered]@{}
foreach ($m in $months) {
  $a = $agg[$m]
  $rev = $a.revenue                              # 3.1.09 refunds are negative, already netted
  $gm  = ($rev + $a.cogs) / $rev * 100           # cogs is negative
  $ebitda = $rev + $a.cogs + $a.sales_marketing + $a.rnd + $a.ga   # 6.x financial excluded
  $res[$m] = [ordered]@{
    revenue = [math]::Round($rev,2); gross_margin_pct = [math]::Round($gm,1); ebitda = [math]::Round($ebitda,2)
    cogs = $a.cogs; sm = $a.sales_marketing; rnd = $a.rnd; ga = $a.ga; fin = $a.financial
  }
  "{0}  rev {1,12:N2}  gm% {2,6:N1}  ebitda {3,12:N2}" -f $m, $rev, $gm, $ebitda
}

# Board definition: burn = average monthly negative EBITDA of last 3 closed months (Apr-Jun)
$last3 = $months[-3..-1] | ForEach-Object { $res[$_].ebitda }
$avg = ($last3 | Measure-Object -Average).Average
Write-Host ("Last3: {0}  avg {1:N2}" -f ($last3 -join ', '), $avg)
$negOnly = $last3 | Where-Object { $_ -lt 0 }
Write-Host ("Negative-only avg: {0:N2}" -f (($negOnly | Measure-Object -Average).Average))

$cash = 1847350.40
$burn = [math]::Abs($avg)
$runway = $cash / $burn
Write-Host ("burn {0:N2}  runway {1:N2}" -f $burn, $runway)
Write-Host ("runway using negative-only {0:N2}" -f ($cash / [math]::Abs(($negOnly | Measure-Object -Average).Average)))

# Sanity: does June closing cash reconcile with May closing + June net movement?
$juneNet = $months[-1]
$n = $agg['2026-06']
$sumAll = 0.0
foreach ($r in $rows) {
  $d = $r.date -split '/'
  if ('{0}-{1}' -f $d[2], $d[1].PadLeft(2,'0') -eq '2026-06') { $sumAll += ToNum $r.amount }
}
Write-Host ("June total ledger movement (all lines): {0:N2}  May cash + this = {1:N2}" -f $sumAll, (2309188.00 + $sumAll))

$out = [ordered]@{ revenue = [ordered]@{}; gross_margin_pct = [ordered]@{}; ebitda = [ordered]@{} }
foreach ($m in $months) {
  $out.revenue[$m] = $res[$m].revenue
  $out.gross_margin_pct[$m] = $res[$m].gross_margin_pct
  $out.ebitda[$m] = $res[$m].ebitda
}
$out['burn'] = [math]::Round($burn,2)
$out['runway_months'] = [math]::Round($runway,2)
$out | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content result.json -Encoding UTF8
Get-Content result.json
